indicators.note: reportedly says we want a word that sounds like the one the clue gives, not its spelling

parts.note: fatter means grosser, more corpulent

explanation.surface: A shopkeeper is said to have put on weight.
explanation.definitionFit: A grocer is a shopkeeper who sells food and household provisions.

parts.note: dour means grim or stern
an ace is a one in cards

explanation.surface: A stern person pulls a face.
explanation.definitionFit: A grimace is a twisted facial expression of pain or disgust.

clue.text: Strange chap holding position as casual worker

parts.note: strange means odd
a job is a post or position
a chap is a man

explanation.surface: A peculiar fellow with a temporary post.
explanation.walkthrough: 'casual worker' is the definition; 'holding' sits between chap and position, so the chap encloses the position.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who does small jobs as they come along is a casual worker.

indicators.note: strange suggests the word is altered into an odd form, its letters reordered

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Bringing up a curious secret.
explanation.definitionFit: To erect something is to put it up or raise it.

definitions.meaning: emotive in the sense of moving, stirring the feelings
fondling is stroking, laying hands on

explanation.surface: Caressing someone stirs the emotions.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses fit: something moving stirs feelings, and the act of handling or feeling with the hands is the other.

indicators.note: turned over in a down clue says the word is flipped end to end

parts.note: ergo is Latin for therefore

explanation.surface: So the beast was flipped onto its back.
explanation.definitionFit: An ogre is a monstrous giant of folklore.

parts.note: cash is money
mere means only, nothing more than

explanation.surface: Funds earmarked only for buying fleece.
explanation.definitionFit: Cashmere is fine wool from the Kashmir goat.

clue.text: I had a house in America

parts.note: I had contracts to I'd

explanation.surface: Someone recalls owning a home in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I had' shortens to I'd, giving ID.
explanation.definitionFit: Idaho is a north-western state located in America.

indicators.note: variety signals a different version, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Collectors seek unusual specimens, valuing larger ones.
explanation.definitionFit: Greater is a comparative meaning larger in size or amount.

parts.note: taken as written
an act or action is a deed

explanation.surface: Someone caught red-handed, certainly in the act.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an emphatic adverb, it is a synonym for truly or certainly.

clue.text: For horse training, get into line on time

indicators.note: in a down-free across clue, on means the second piece follows the first

parts.note: to dress ranks is the military order to line up straight
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Instructions to line up promptly for an equestrian session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dress' is the parade-ground command to align ranks, which is why 'get into line' gives it.
explanation.definitionFit: Dressage is the discipline of training a horse to perform precise movements.

parts.note: re means about, concerning
a quest is a search or hunt

explanation.surface: Enquiring about a search party.
explanation.definitionFit: To request is to ask for something politely.

indicators.note: arranged says the letters of the following words are set out in a new order

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Followers lay the dinner plates in a particular way.
explanation.definitionFit: The twelve apostles were the chosen disciples of Jesus.

definitions.meaning: goods brought into a country from abroad

explanation.surface: Asking how much an imported item really matters.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both weight or meaning and goods bought from overseas, two distinct senses.

clue.text: Go in and use arrangement relating to fire

indicators.note: arrangement says letters of the preceding words are set out afresh

parts.note: fodder taken as written
fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Instructions for entering and using a fireplace.
explanation.definitionFit: Igneous means of fire; igneous rocks formed from molten magma.

clue.text: Some of them made friends with girl

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A few of them befriended a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'friends with girl' as the definition, but that phrase does not define a name; 'girl' alone does, and 'friends with' is surface padding joining it.
explanation.definitionFit: Emma is a girl's first name, so it stands for a girl in crossword style.

clue.text: Bird has to shift gear on a river

parts.note: to budge is to shift or move
rig means equipment or gear

explanation.surface: A cyclist changes gear on a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'gear' is not anagram fodder here: it is RIG, kit or equipment.
explanation.definitionFit: A budgerigar is a small Australian parakeet, a common pet bird.

clue.text: Dug soil all over the place, covering the French plant

indicators.note: covering says one piece wraps around the other
all over the place says the letters are scattered into a new order

parts.note: la is a French word for the

explanation.surface: Digging the earth everywhere to bed in a French flower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'all over the place' turns DUG SOIL into GDIOLUS, and 'covering' wraps it around LA.
explanation.definitionFit: The gladiolus is a flowering plant with sword-shaped leaves.

parts.note: Black is one of the two sides in chess
out is the opposite of in

explanation.surface: A chess opponent has lapsed into unconsciousness.
explanation.definitionFit: A blackout is a loss of consciousness, much like a brief coma.

parts.note: warbled means sang, giving sung
lasses are girls

explanation.surface: Women in sunglasses singing a song.
explanation.definitionFit: Shades is an informal word for dark spectacles worn against bright light.

clue.text: Thin transmitter with small line inside

indicators.note: inside says one piece goes within the other

parts.note: a sender transmits a message or signal
L is the short form, a small abbreviation, of line

explanation.surface: A slim device for broadcasting with a narrow wire inside.
explanation.definitionFit: Slender means slim or thin.

indicators.note: almost says the word is not quite complete, its final letter dropped

parts.note: prehistoric means very early, from the earliest times

explanation.surface: An ancient aristocrat is very nearly a fossil.
explanation.definitionFit: An earl is a British nobleman ranking above a viscount.

clue.text: A flat-bottomed barge is not as heavy

definitions.meaning: a barge used to unload ships in harbour

explanation.surface: Comparing the weight of a cargo boat.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names a harbour barge and is also the comparative of light in weight.

definitions.meaning: trim in the sense of neat and smart
an evergreen conifer of the pine family

explanation.surface: Pruning a pine-like tree.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means neat and smart in appearance, and also names an evergreen conifer.

clue.text: Persuade dithering niece to include tenor

indicators.note: to include says one piece is put inside the other
dithering suggests confused movement, so the word's letters are jumbled

parts.note: T is a standard abbreviation for tenor in music

explanation.surface: Coaxing an indecisive niece to bring a singer along.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dithering' jumbles NIECE into ENICE, and 'to include' puts T inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To entice is to lure or tempt someone into doing something, which is to persuade.

clue.text: Opera partly geared to Scarpia's plotting

indicators.note: partly says the answer is a part of the words that follow

explanation.surface: A work whose plot is shaped around the villain Scarpia's scheming.
explanation.walkthrough: Scarpia is the villainous police chief of this very opera, so the surface fits it.
explanation.definitionFit: Tosca is an opera by Puccini.

parts.note: to dump something is to get rid of it
ling is another name for common heather

explanation.surface: Discarding Heather's dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: Heather looks like a woman's name; it is the plant, also called ling.
explanation.definitionFit: A suet dumpling served with sweet sauce is a traditional British pudding.

parts.note: the feminine pronoun is her rather than him

explanation.definitionFit: A hero is a champion or celebrated defender of a cause.

parts.note: a disc is a gramophone record
over means finished, at an end

clue.text: Not at home to authorise opening

parts.note: someone not at home is out
to let is to permit or authorise

clue.text: Funnily, I care not for the response

parts.note: fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: An offhand shrug in answer to a question.
explanation.definitionFit: A reaction is how someone responds to something.

clue.text: Man said to make water heater

indicators.note: said says the answer sounds like the word for man

parts.note: geezer is British slang for a man or bloke

explanation.surface: A fellow apparently building a boiler.
explanation.walkthrough: In British English the two words sound alike, and a gas water heater is commonly called a geyser; geezer is informal British slang for a man.
explanation.definitionFit: In Britain a geyser is a gas appliance that heats water on demand.
